title: C Y P two C nine and warfarin

segs.text: Section eleven. C Y P two C nine, warfarin, and the narrow therapeutic index drugs. This enzyme matters because it metabolizes several drugs where a small change in clearance changes the outcome. She said, it does metabolism of a lot of our very narrow therapeutic index drugs, so things like warfarin that we've already talked to some about, and then phenytoin and glipizide. Tolbutamide is on the same list.

The two common variants both reduce function, and star three is the more severe loss. In her numbers, C Y P two C nine star two keeps about twenty percent of wild type activity, and star three keeps about five percent. The Katzung chapter states it differently, as a thirty to forty percent and an eighty to ninety percent reduction in S warfarin metabolism.

Warfarin is cleared by C Y P two C nine, so a low activity variant clears it slowly and the drug builds up. The starting dose must be lowered, not raised, to keep this anticoagulant out of the bleeding range.

Two separate studies point the same way. One measured clearance and found a gene dose effect. People with two copies of star three had about a ninety percent reduction in S warfarin clearance compared with people with two copies of star one. The other looked at who needed the lowest starting dose. The usual start is about five milligrams per day, and the lowest dose patients need about one point five milligrams per day. She said, at least eighty percent of the people in that dosing category have these low activity variants of two C nine. The dosing data strengthened the clearance data.

The variants are not equally common. About thirty percent of Caucasians carry a low activity variant, about one to three percent of African Americans, and about zero percent of East Asians in the population studied. C Y P two C nine is also inhibited by many drugs. An inhibitor lowers its activity, and a low activity variant lowers it further. The two add up rather than cancel, so a substrate can reach concentrations that are too high.
